title: University education
subtitle: do a degree, lectures, postgraduate
summary: Talk about university subjects, getting a degree and going on to a Master's or a PhD.

lesson.heading: Subjects and the jobs they lead to
rows: a businessman or businesswoman (you go into business)
lesson.note: You do or study a subject at university.

lesson.heading: Getting a place and getting a degree
lesson.text: Some students go to university because they enjoy studying; others just want a **qualification**. First you have to get good **grades** in your final school exams to **get a place** at university. Then you **study for** (or **do**) **a degree**.

examples.text: I got very good **grades** in my final school exams.
I **got a place** at university to do economics.
If you complete the course successfully, you **get your degree** and receive a **certificate**.
Most degree courses **last** three years, although some take longer, e.g. medicine or law.

lesson.heading: Lecturers and lectures
lesson.text: Teachers at university are usually called **lecturers**, and most of the teaching is done through **lectures**: the lecturer talks and the students listen. The most senior lecturers have the title **Professor**.

examples.text: Our **lecturer** is very good; I never miss her **lectures**.

left.label: Arts subjects
examples: They spend time working in the **library**.

right.label: Science subjects
examples: They spend a lot of time working in a **laboratory**.
*Lab* is the informal word for a laboratory.

lesson.heading: Undergraduates, graduates and postgraduates
lesson.text: While students are doing their first degree, they are **undergraduates**. When they complete it, they are **graduates**. Some graduates **go on to do** a **Master's**, e.g. an MA (Master of Arts) or MSc (Master of Science). These are **postgraduate degrees**.

examples.text: He **went on to do** an MSc.
The longest postgraduate degree is a **PhD**, where students do **research** for at least three years.
examples.note: research = a detailed study of one particular subject

lesson.text: We **do** a degree and **get** a degree, but we **go to** university - not ~~go to the university~~.

exercises.prompt: Match the subject with the job it leads to.
To become a doctor you need to study ___.
exercises.explanation: Medicine is the university subject for future doctors.

exercises.prompt: Students who are still studying for their first degree are called ___.
exercises.explanation: You are an undergraduate until you complete your first degree; then you are a graduate.

exercises.prompt: If you study arts subjects such as English or history, where do you spend a lot of your time?
exercises.explanation: Arts students work in the library and write essays; science students work in a laboratory.

exercises.statement: At an English university, the teachers are all called professors.
exercises.explanation: Most teachers at university are called lecturers. Only the most senior ones have the title Professor.

exercises.statement: Most university degree courses in the UK last two years.
exercises.explanation: Most degree courses last three years, and some, such as medicine or law, take longer.

exercises.statement: A PhD is a postgraduate degree.
exercises.explanation: Correct. You do a PhD after your first degree, and it takes at least three years of research.

exercises.prompt: Stephen got very good ___ in his final school exams, so he got a place at university.
exercises.explanation: You need good grades in your school exams to get a place at university.

exercises.prompt: He went to university and got a ___ in economics.
exercises.explanation: A degree is the qualification you get when you complete a university course.

exercises.prompt: The MSc course ___ a year, and at the end of it he had a job offer.
exercises.explanation: A course lasts a year = it continues for a year.

exercises.prompt: He went back to university to do ___ for a PhD.
exercises.explanation: Research is a detailed study of one particular subject.

exercises.prompt: Is the word about the first degree or about study after it?
Say what some students do after their first degree.
exercises.answer: Some graduates go on to do a Master's.
exercises.explanation: Go on to do something = do it next, after what you have just finished.
